traps.shape: when the caller opts into following redirects, the redirect chain is handed to the network client, so a later hop is requested without any address check; the manual branch's guard was written for one hop and never existed for the auto-followed ones
traps.where: index.ts:424 (redirect option), index.ts:428-430 (fetch), index.ts:439-462 (manual branch that does hold a check)
traps.reason_to_dismiss: following redirects is an explicitly opted-in mode the README documents as insecure, so a caller that turns it on has accepted redirect risk; the loopback block was written for the manual branch

traps.shape: the address the caller's resolver reports is classified by a dotted-quad regex, so IPv6 forms (loopback, mapped, compatible, NAT64, ULA, link-local, zoned) and the unspecified address pass as public; an answer that is not an address at all also passes
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the documented resolver returns node's dns.lookup answer, normally an IPv4 dotted quad, and the regex covers every range the README names, so the check reads as complete

traps.shape: the answer is checked but the name is resolved again when the request is made, so the request can reach an address the check never saw; the checked address is not the address of the connection
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the library already resolves the host and throws on a private answer before fetching, so the guard appears to be in place and a name that answers differently on the next lookup is the caller's resolver's problem
traps.realistic_because: the advisory's own route, unmodified upstream code

traps.shape: the redirect target's answer is checked immediately before the second request, which resolves the target name again, so the second request can reach an address the check never saw
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the target is resolved and checked right before the second request and the caller's approval function had to accept it, so the hop reads as guarded
traps.realistic_because: the advisory's own route, unmodified upstream code

traps.shape: a link whose own host is an address is filtered by a list that covers only 10/127/169.254/192.168/172.16-31, so the carrier-grade NAT, documentation and benchmark ranges the library's own guard calls non-public are accepted and requested
traps.where: constants.ts:9-37 (link detector), constants.ts:40-68 (the guard's own list of non-public ranges)
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the outer expression is only a link detector, and the ranges it omits are not the classic internal-service hosts, so the gap looks academic

wrong_fix_catalogue.crash_as_refusal: n/a: the refusal form is a rejected promise with no status channel, so a throwing fix is indistinguishable from a clean refusal at this API; the functional suite is what catches a refusal that also hits legitimate callers
wrong_fix_catalogue.wrong_resource: n/a: the protection is over addresses, not over resources; there is no neighbouring object a check could authorise instead
wrong_fix_catalogue.one_role_or_direction: n/a: the library only fetches, in one direction, for one kind of caller; there is no second role or verb to leave unfixed
wrong_fix_catalogue.reads_only: n/a: the library has no separate read and write paths; every route that matters is the same fetch
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: no authority, secret or role lookup exists in this product; the resolver hook is the only authority and it is always consulted
